record.paper_title: Orthogonality Types in Normed Linear Spaces
record.original_question: Let X be a normed space of dimension at least 3. Height orthogonality x ⊥_H y is the relation in which either x = 0 or y = 0, or ∥x - y∥ equals ∥(∥y∥/∥x∥)x + (∥x∥/∥y∥)y∥. What can be concluded if height orthogonality is homogeneous in X, meaning x ⊥_H y implies x ⊥_H λy for every scalar λ? Does this force an inner product norm, the π/2-property on all two-dimensional subspaces, or another classification?

evidence.quote: Question 4.9.37 What happens if dim X ≥ 3, and height orthogonality is homogeneous?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a real normed linear space with $\dim X \ge 3$. For $x, y \in X$, say that $x$ is height-orthogonal to $y$, written $x \perp_H y$, if either $x = 0$, or $y = 0$, or
$$\|x - y\| = \left\| \tfrac{\|y\|}{\|x\|}\,x + \tfrac{\|x\|}{\|y\|}\,y \right\|.$$
(Geometrically, in the plane spanned by $x$ and $y$, this says that the segment from $x$ to $y$ has the same length as the segment joining the points on the rays through $x$ and $y$ at suitably scaled positions, expressing that the "height" from one vertex equals a prescribed length.)

The relation $\perp_H$ is called homogeneous on $X$ if for all $x, y \in X$ and every scalar $\lambda$,
$$x \perp_H y \;\Longrightarrow\; x \perp_H \lambda y.$$

Assuming that height orthogonality is homogeneous on $X$, determine which structural conclusions follow. In particular: must the norm on $X$ be induced by an inner product? Equivalently, must every two-dimensional subspace of $X$ have the $\pi/2$-property (i.e., for every nonzero $x$ in a 2-dimensional subspace $Y$ there exists $y \in Y$ with $x \perp_H y$ and the angle between $x$ and $y$ is a right angle in the inner-product sense)? Provide a complete classification of normed spaces of dimension $\ge 3$ on which height orthogonality is homogeneous.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not turn up a published resolution of the homogeneity question for height orthogonality in normed spaces of dimension at least 3. While analogous homogeneity-implies-inner-product characterizations are known for several other orthogonality types (e.g., isosceles, Pythagorean, Birkhoff–James in various settings), no source verifying or refuting the corresponding statement for height orthogonality was located, so the status is treated as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Orthogonality in Normed Spaces - ScholarWorks@CWU
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys orthogonality types in normed spaces and their homogeneity, symmetry, and additivity properties; height orthogonality's homogeneity question is not resolved here.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the homogeneity question for height orthogonality is reported in standard surveys of orthogonality types.

status_evidence.title: Area orthogonality in normed linear spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses geometric orthogonalities in normed spaces (e.g., area orthogonality), illustrating typical homogeneity-implies-inner-product results for related but distinct notions.
status_evidence.claim: Analogous classification results exist for related orthogonality notions, but no specific result for height orthogonality was found.
